name: Garage Management
description: The housing category's answer for a game where home is a garage: multi-vehicle ownership, part installation, and visual customization under one roof. It owns the roster of owned vehicles, which one is currently deployed, and the act of installing a purchased part — expressed as a new preset on that vehicle's movement.vehicle_tuning sheet, so an engine swap and a tune change travel the same code path and nothing bypasses the tuning contract. Money never touches this component: it listens for economy.spent and installs what the receipt describes, which keeps refunds, insufficient funds, and pricing entirely in economy.currency's audit trail. Entry and exit (movement.vehicleEntered / movement.vehicleExited) tell it when the deployed vehicle is actually in use, which is what makes 'you cannot sell the car you are sitting in' a rule instead of a bug report. It does not own the race, the drive, or the driver's skills — progression.driver_progression is the person; this is the metal.

inputs.name: maxVehicleSlots
inputs.description: Roster size. A hard cap is what makes pink-slip wins meaningful — taking a rival's car forces a decision about your own.

inputs.name: installRequiresStored
inputs.description: When true, parts can only be installed on a stored vehicle. Wrenching on the car mid-race is not a build strategy this genre supports.

inputs.name: customizationSlots
inputs.description: Visual customization categories per vehicle. Purely cosmetic: if a slot changed performance it would be a part, not a customization.

outputs.name: installedParts
outputs.description: Vehicle id to installed part list. Read by shop UI to grey out duplicates and by resale logic to value a modified car.
